title: Avoid using deprecated Buffer constructor
body:
This pull request addresses the use of deprecated `Buffer` constructors in several runtime dependencies by applying targeted patches and adding automated tests to ensure compliance. It also introduces `patch-package` as a dependency and configures it to run automatically after installation.

**Dependency modernization and maintenance:**

* Added `patch-package` as a dependency and configured it to run automatically after install via the `postinstall` script in `package.json`. This ensures that necessary patches are always applied to dependencies after installation.

**Patching runtime dependencies to avoid deprecated Buffer usage:**

* Added patch files for `binary`, `buffers`, `tunnel`, and `unzip-stream` packages to replace deprecated `new Buffer()` and similar patterns with the recommended `Buffer.from()` and `Buffer.alloc()` APIs, ensuring compatibility with newer Node.js versions and preventing deprecation warnings or errors. 

**Testing and validation:**

* Introduced a new test suite (`__tests__/dependencies.test.ts`) that verifies the patched dependencies (`unzip-stream`, `binary`, `buffers`, and `tunnel`) do not trigger deprecated Buffer warnings or errors when run with strict deprecation flags, ensuring the effectiveness of the applied patches.

title: "Resource not accessible by integration" does not say which permission is missing
body:
## Summary

Downloading an artifact from another workflow run with `run-id` fails with:

```
Unable to download artifact(s): Resource not accessible by integration
```

That is the raw API response for a token missing a scope. It does not name the scope. The answer is `actions: read`.

## Why it is hard to find

The README covers `actions:read` only in [Download Artifacts from other Workflow Runs or Repositories](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact#download-artifacts-from-other-workflow-runs-or-repositories), in a code comment next to `secrets.GH_PAT`:

```yaml
github-token: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }} # token with actions:read permissions on target repo
```

That reads as a cross-repository concern. The same requirement applies **within one repository** when `run-id` is used with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, because `actions: read` is not granted once a workflow declares its own `permissions:` block.

Searching this repository's issues for the error string returns nothing, so there is no landing page for someone who pastes it into a search box.

## How it showed up for me

A nightly workflow uploads `test-results-json`. A second workflow downloads it with `run-id` and builds a GitHub issue listing which tests failed.

That download step had `continue-on-error: true`, so the failure never surfaced. For weeks the issue said *"12 tests failed"* with *"(no test-results JSON available)"* underneath, which is close to useless for whoever picks it up. The artifact existed the whole time, 18900 bytes, not expired.

Adding `actions: read` fixed it immediately. Finding that took a lot longer than fixing it.

## Proposed fix

PR #488 is open, with tests. It leaves the message alone for unrelated errors and appends the permission and the exact block to add when the API returns this specific error.

No attachment to the wording. If you would rather solve it in the README, or phrase it differently, that works just as well for the next person who hits it.

title: Name the missing permission when the token cannot read artifacts
body:
## The problem

Downloading an artifact from another workflow run fails with:

```
Unable to download artifact(s): Resource not accessible by integration
```

That is the raw API response for a token missing a scope, and it does not say which scope. The answer is `actions: read`, which is not granted once a workflow declares its own `permissions:` block.

The README documents `actions:read` [in the cross-repository example](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact#download-artifacts-from-other-workflow-runs-or-repositories), next to a PAT, which reads as a different-repo concern. The same requirement applies **inside a single repository** when `run-id` is used with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and that is where it is most likely to be hit.

## How I ran into it

A nightly workflow uploads `test-results-json`, and a second workflow downloads it with `run-id` to build a GitHub issue listing the failing tests.

The download step had `continue-on-error: true`, so the failure was swallowed and the issue shipped for weeks saying *"12 tests failed"* with the line *"(no test-results JSON available)"* underneath. The artifact existed the whole time. The message gave nothing to search for, and searching this repository's issues for it returns nothing either.

## The change

```
Unable to download artifact(s): Resource not accessible by integration

This usually means the token is missing the `actions: read` permission,
which is required to read artifacts from another workflow run.

If the job declares a `permissions:` block, add:

    permissions:
      actions: read

For an artifact in a different repository, the `github-token` input needs
a token with `actions:read` on that repository. See the README section
"Download Artifacts from other Workflow Runs or Repositories".
```

Unrelated errors pass through unchanged.

## Tests

Four, on the extracted `describeDownloadFailure`:

| Case | Expected |
|---|---|
| `Resource not accessible by integration` | hint added |
| Same, different casing | hint added |
| `Artifact 'build' not found` | unchanged, no hint |
| `Resource not found` | no hint (not the same failure) |

I also checked the tests can actually fail: forcing the branch to never add the hint turns two of them red, and reverting turns them green again. A test that cannot fail is not a test.

## Checklist from CONTRIBUTING

- `npm run test` — 25 passed (21 before, 4 added)
- `npm run format` — unchanged
- `npm run lint` — clean
- `npm run release` — `dist/index.js` rebuilt, hint verified present in the bundle
- `npm run check-all` — all green

Happy to reword the message, or to drop the cross-repository paragraph if you would rather keep it to one line.

title: v8 emits Node DEP0005 Buffer() deprecation warning on every download
body:
### What happened

`actions/download-artifact@v8` emits this warning on GitHub-hosted runners while downloading ordinary workflow artifacts:

```text
(node:...) [DEP0005] DeprecationWarning: Buffer() is deprecated due to security and usability issues. Please use the Buffer.alloc(), Buffer.allocUnsafe(), or Buffer.from() methods instead.
```

A current public reproduction is the `Download checksum fragments` step in https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/29465138404.

### Minimal workflow

```yaml
- uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
  with:
    pattern: checksums-*
    path: fragments
    merge-multiple: true
```

### Root cause evidence

The v8 bundle includes `@actions/artifact@6.2.1`, whose extraction dependency chain reaches `unzip-stream@0.3.4` -> `binary@0.3.0` / `buffers@0.1.1`; the bundled JavaScript still calls the deprecated `Buffer()` constructor. GitHub Actions now executes the action on Node 24, which surfaces DEP0005.

### Suggested fix

Upgrade or replace the extraction dependency chain and regenerate `dist/` so it contains no `Buffer()` constructor calls. A regression test can execute a small artifact download with `NODE_OPTIONS=--throw-deprecation` (or scan the generated bundle) to prevent recurrence.

title: [feat req] Add download progress logging to actions/download-artifact
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Please add download progress logging to `actions/download-artifact`.

Currently, when downloading large artifacts, the action produces no intermediate output until completion. From the workflow logs, it appears “stuck” even though data is actively being transferred.

It would be very helpful if the action could emit periodic progress information to stdout, for example:

* Downloaded bytes vs total size
* Percentage completed (if available)
* Periodic status logs (e.g., every N MB or every few seconds)
* Optional `show-progress` or `verbose` flag

Even minimal progress logging would significantly improve usability.


### Why is this needed?

For large artifacts or slower networks, downloads can take several minutes with zero log output. This makes it difficult to distinguish between:

* A healthy but slow download
* A stalled job
* A networking issue

As a result:

* CI logs look frozen
* Debugging becomes harder
* Developers often assume the workflow is hung

Adding progress output would:

* Improve observability in CI pipelines
* Reduce false-positive job cancellations
* Make troubleshooting much easier
* Improve overall developer experience

This is especially important in production pipelines where artifacts can be hundreds of MB or larger.

title: [bug] When downloading all artifacts but there is only a single one, no subdir is created.
body:
I am running into a bug after upgrading from v4 to v7 because of the [change in v5](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact?tab=readme-ov-file#v5---whats-new) by @GrantBirki

https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/blob/37930b1c2abaa49bbe596cd826c3c89aef350131/README.md?plain=1#L42-L47

However there was also an unmentioned change __when downloading all artifacts__ i.e. not specifying a given name or id. The documentation says that in this case a directory will be created for each artifact:



https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/blob/37930b1c2abaa49bbe596cd826c3c89aef350131/README.md?plain=1#L213-L225

And the log says the same:

```
No input name, artifact-ids or pattern filtered specified, downloading all artifacts
An extra directory with the artifact name will be created for each download
Preparing to download the following artifacts:
...
```

However  __this is not what is happening!__ If we download all artifacts, but there happens to be only one, __it does not create the subdirectories anymore__ and all files are extracted into the root dir.

This is a bug: when we need all artifacts and we do not give a specific a name or id, and we use the default `merge-multiple: false` then the correct behavior is creating a subdirectory per artifact, regardless of how many there are.

## Problem

My workflow generates a __variable number of artifacts__. Usually it is quite a few, but sometimes just a single. We don't know in advance.

The deploy step __downloads all of the artifacts into their own directory__, and iterates over them to deploy each of them. However as of `download-artifact@v7` the behavior became inconsistent for the case when there was just a single artifact, because `download-artifact` no longer creates a directory but instead extracts all the files from the single artifact into the working dir.

This is unfortunate in my case because I don't know in advance how many artifacts we will have. Is there a way to mimic the old v4 behavior: download all artifacts, each into it's own dir. Even when there is only one?



### Why is this needed?

In case of a dynamic number of artifacts, the `download-artifact@v7` special behavior for the n=1 case is inconsistent and causes programming errors.

title: [docs] Action always creates subdirectory when using `artifact-ids`
body:
### What files would you like to change?

https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/blob/448e3f862ab3ef47aa50ff917776823c9946035b/README.md?plain=1#L75-L78
https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/blob/448e3f862ab3ef47aa50ff917776823c9946035b/README.md?plain=1#L144-L169

### What are your suggested changes?

When you are using the input `artifact-ids` (instead of `name`), the action always creates a subdirectory with the name of the artifact. Specifically, the action creates a subdirectory even when downloading a single artifact.

This is a significant difference in behavior compared with the usage of `name`. This means uses of `name` cannot just be replaced with `artifact-ids` without also adding `merge-multiple: true`. The deviation in behavior should be highlighted in the documentation of `artifact-ids`.

The documentation of `merge-multiple` is now also slightly misleading as it changes the behavior even if downloading a single artifact.

> When multiple artifacts are matched, this changes the behavior of the destination directories.
> — Documentation of `merge-multiple`

The section [“Download Artifacts by ID” in the README.md](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/blob/448e3f862ab3ef47aa50ff917776823c9946035b/README.md#download-artifacts-by-id) is also misleading as it suggests that artifacts are downloaded into separate directories only if multiple IDs are specified.

> Multiple artifacts can be downloaded by providing a comma-separated list of IDs:
> [...]
> This will download multiple artifacts to separate directories (similar to downloading multiple artifacts by name).

I wasn't sure whether to report this as a bug or a documentation issue. However, since changing the behavior now would probably be problematic and risk breaking existing usages, I assumed updating the documentation is the only acceptable resolution. I also think changing the target directory depending on the amount of artifacts specified via `artifact-ids` would also not be ideal.

title: feat: add support for unzip argument in downloadArtifact
body:
This PR just add the possibility to filter what we want to unzip or not when downloading artifacts.

This feature was asked by so many people, and the implementation change almost nothing in the code. So it won't break any part of the action.

Here a simple example that show how it work : https://github.com/shiipou/download-artifact/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

You can also try it with this workflow : 

<details>

<summary>Workflow</summary>

```yml
name: Loop Over Artifact IDs

on: [push]

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: write
  packages: write

jobs:
  create-artifacts:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Create and upload artifacts
        run: |
          mkdir -p artifact1 artifact2
          echo "Content1" > artifact1/file.txt
          echo "Content2.1" > artifact2/file1.txt
          echo "Content2.2" > artifact2/file2.txt
          echo "Content2.3" > artifact2/file3.txt
      - id: artifact-1
        name: Upload artifact 1
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: artifact1
          path: artifact1/*
      - id: artifact-2
        name: Upload artifact 2
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: artifact2
          path: artifact2/*
    outputs:
      artifact-1-id: ${{ steps.artifact-1.outputs.artifact-id }}
      artifact-2-id: ${{ steps.artifact-2.outputs.artifact-id }}

  process-artifacts:
    needs: create-artifacts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: download-artifacts
        name: Download artifacts
        uses: shiipou/download-artifact@main
        with:
          artifact-ids: ${{ needs.create-artifacts.outputs.artifact-1-id }},${{ needs.create-artifacts.outputs.artifact-2-id }}
          path: artifacts/
          unzip: ${{ needs.create-artifacts.outputs.artifact-1-id }}
      - name: print artifacts
        run: ls -pAR artifacts/
      - name: unzip artifacts
        run: unzip artifacts/**/*.zip
```

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7bf76499-0482-49bc-b9ab-6c1ffde44105)

</details>

This PR need this (https://github.com/actions/toolkit/pull/2095) to be merged before.

This simply add a new `unzip` input, this input take as value : artefact-ids, artefact-names, true, false, or '*'.

- `artefact-ids` will be a comma separated string of artifact's ids we want to unzip  
- `artefact-names` will be a comma separated string of artefact's names we want to unzip
- `true` is used to unzip everything
- `false` is used to keep everything zipped
- `*` is used to unzip everything

Hey :wave:

I would like to better connect two jobs/steps of `actions/upload-artifact` and `actions/download-artifact`. Therefore, it would  be very useful if the outputs of the former could be used as input for the latter.

Taking the `artifact-id` as an example. A exemplary workflow with two jobs (could be also just two steps within a job) could then look like this. This also includes the "hints" how to do it now (?).

```yaml
# Trigger & Co.

jobs:
  job1:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      artifact-id: ${{ steps.upload.outputs.artifact-id }}
      
    steps:
      - name: do something that can be uploaded then
        run: echo foo > bar.txt
        
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        id: upload
        with:
          path: ./bar.txt
          name: important-asset # simple static name for linking

  job2:
    needs: job1
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          artifact-id: ${{ needs.job1.outputs.artifact-id }}
          # how to do it now --> name: important-asset
          path: ./can-be-found-here
          
      - name: do something with the downloaded asset
        run: stat ./can-be-found-here
```

### Why is this needed?

Strong, verifiable, auto-completable relationship between these two related actions. Potentially supporting more complex scenarios where simple copy-code `name`s do not work.

### What would you like to be added?

Add an input that sets the timeout for the action to succedd

### Why is this needed?

title: Add allow-not-found input argument
body:
Closes #42

This PR adds the `allow-not-found` input argument to `download-artifact` that, when set to `true`, will not fail the action when an artifact with the specified `name` input argument is not found.

If the artifact is not found, the output of `download-path` of the action will contain an empty string instead of the would-be download path. This can be checked in the subsequent step via `${{ steps.<id>.outputs.download-path != '' }}` as can be seen in the updated workflow test.yml file. Additionally, a warning is printed via `core.warning` if the artifact is not found while `allow-not-found` is set to true.

If `allow-not-found` is set to false (default behavior), the action behaves as it did before this PR.

title: Support mapping failures to an output
body:
### What would you like to be added?

add a `warn-on-failure` to suppress the failure status to enable composite actions not to die when an artifact in the current job isn't available

### Why is this needed?

I'm maintaining a complicated action. In actions/download-artifact@v3, running a workflow with a matrix, the outputs for each job would be merged, and if one job didn't produce an output, its absence would be folded into the single artifact (and as long as at least one leg in the matrix produced an artifact, there'd be an artifact).

The workflow/action could then fan out and retrieve the single artifact (in each fan), and if the specific job produced an output, it would be included in the data, and it could do what it wanted to do.

In v4, each fanned element has to independently produce an artifact, on the other side, each receiver has to also fan out and _expect_ that there will *definitely* be an artifact produced for its fanned element. If there isn't, then actions/download-artifact@v4 will fail, the action will fail (individual subsequent steps can work around the failure) and the job will fail unless lots of annoying steps are taken to handle the failure (`if: failure()`) from the step (but how would a workflow know if it should ignore the failure from the action? that's insane).

In composite jobs, a fatal uses: statement appears quite fatal (unless someone documents a way to make them not fatal):
- [x] https://github.com/github/docs/issues/31356

I've implemented this feature in order to make my action not require `actions: read` (which `gh run download` requires)
https://github.com/check-spelling/check-spelling/commit/abe1dea90ec688aae64c23a5f5ccbb28043f37e7

If `gh run download` allowed downloading current workflow run artifacts w/o `actions: read`, then I could work around this deficiency, but at present, I can't:
- [x] https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/8641

Having to add `actions: read` to each workflow consumer is fairly onerous (I've added code for it as well: https://github.com/check-spelling/check-spelling/commit/0acd92b5ce903362fdfa1e016595df2008f5c1de).

title: [feat req] Option to download an individual file from an artifact
body:
### What would you like to be added?

An option that allows you to download a specific file from an artifact.

So f.e. defining a workflow step like
```yaml
- uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
  with:
    name: some-artifact
    file: some-file.txt
```
would download `some-file.txt` from the artifact `some-artifact`

### Why is this needed?

There are cases where you want to save multiple files into a single artifact to not have to make multiple steps uploading each one individually for later usage in a different job.
The issue is, that the action, as of right now, is just downloading the artifact as a whole, meaning it also loads files that may not be needed by the specific step in the end, as it's basically bloat that will be discarded at the end.

As an example, assuming we want to use a Matrix setup to deal with each individual file (i.e. upload them to different platforms), while creating said files should only be done once by having it as a separate job, creating multiple files like this
```yaml
jobs:
  createFiles:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    - run: mkdir -p path/to/artifact
    - run: echo Platform 1 > path/to/artifact/platform_1.txt
    - run: echo Platform 1 > path/to/artifact/platform_2.txt
    - run: echo Platform 1 > path/to/artifact/platform_3.txt
    - run: echo Platform 1 > path/to/artifact/platform_4.txt
```
would require one of multiple solutions:

1. Multiple artefacts:
   ```yaml
   jobs:
     createFiles:
       runs-on: ubuntu-latest
       steps:
       # Creating files
       - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
         with:
           name: my-artifact-1
           path: path/to/artifact/platform_1.txt
       - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
         with:
           name: my-artifact-2
           path: path/to/artifact/platform_2.txt
       - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
         with:
           name: my-artifact-3
           path: path/to/artifact/platform_3.txt
       - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
         with:
           name: my-artifact-4
           path: path/to/artifact/platform_4.txt
     publishFiles:
       runs-on: ubuntu-latest
       strategy:
         matrix:
           include:
           - platform: 1
           - platform: 2
           - platform: 3
           - platform: 4
       steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v3
       - uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
         with:
           name: my-artifact-${{ matrix.platform }}
       - uses: example/example-publish@v1 # Mockup action
         with:
           # Assuming the action supports Glob patterns, 'platform_?.txt' can be used to simplify things
           file: platform_?.txt
   ```
   Downside is that it obviously has multiple steps to create multiple artefacts which isn't optimal, but would allow a relatively simple handling of the file in follow-up steps.

2. One artifact:
   ```yaml
   jobs:
     createFiles:
       runs-on: ubuntu-latest
       steps:
       # Creating files
       - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
         with:
           name: my-artifact
           path: path/to/artifact/platform_?.txt
     publishFiles:
       runs-on: ubuntu-latest
       strategy:
         matrix:
           include:
           - platform: 1
           - platform: 2
           - platform: 3
           - platform: 4
       steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v3
       - uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
         with:
           name: my-artifact
       - uses: example/example-publish@v1 # Mockup action
         with:
           # Assuming the action supports Glob patterns, this won't work with 'platform_?.txt'
           file: platform_${{ matrix.platform }}.txt
   ```
   A downside here is, that the entire artefact is downloaded. For TXT files may this not be that big of a deal, but depending on what is uploaded as an artefact can this cause several MBs of data to be downloaded in the end for just one to actually be used.

3. The idea:
   ```yaml
   jobs:
     createFiles:
       runs-on: ubuntu-latest
       steps:
       # Creating files
       - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
         with:
           name: my-artifact
           path: path/to/artifact/platform_?.txt
     publishFiles:
       runs-on: ubuntu-latest
       strategy:
         matrix:
           include:
           - platform: 1
           - platform: 2
           - platform: 3
           - platform: 4
       steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v3
       - uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
         with:
           name: my-artifact
           file: platform_${{ matrix.platform }}.txt
       - uses: example/example-publish@v1 # Mockup action
         with:
           # Thanks to the above option, glob patterns can be used here again.
           file: platform_?.txt
   ```

I'm not sure if the example I gave really shows the benefits. I'm sure there are other, more complex examples that would justify such an option to be present.
Of course, this also depends on if the way download-artifact works are making a targeted download of specific files possible.

In the end, the main benefit would be to keep files in one artefact without having to download not needed ones from an artifact, only to discard them at the end.

title: [feat req] v4 do not use artifact name in paths
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Currently, if "name" is not specified, the download action creates additional dirs when unpacking files. So when you upload a file like this.

```yaml
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
  with:
    path: path/to/artifact/world.txt
```
And then download like this,
```yaml
- uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
```
You will get `artifact/world.txt` instead of `world.txt` in current dir.

I propose simplified v4 logic for both upload and download, with identical behavior, just like working with standard archives.

```yaml
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    pathroot: path/to/artifact
    filefilter: world.txt
    archroot: docs
```

```yaml
- uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
  with:
    pathroot: dist
    filefilter: docs/world.txt
```

These two actions pass `path/to/artifact/world.txt` from one job to `dist/docs/world.txt` in another.

Subdirs are explicitly used to separate files from different jobs in one run. That's not using artifact name like it is now sometimes prepended to output dir and sometimes not.

The same `filefilter:` is used for both compressing and extracting. This avoids tracking where magic pattern ends, to understand where your files will end up both during compression and extraction.

If users have to specify root dir in archive with `archroot:`, then they could accidentally overwrite files that are already added. The default behavior for overwriting files that are already present would be to fail, unless `overwrite: true` is set.

### Why is this needed?

Learning upload/download path handling is hard. Usually it requires a few manual CI runs. Normalizing logic to be similar with how users work with archives will help more people get this right from the first try (and understand what is going on in terms of errors). This could be immediately solve #103, #165, #138, #105, and well, perhaps some of the older issues that may have been already addressed by v2 and v3.

If I understand right, currently only `jobs` can `need` _(wait)_ for other `jobs` to finish.

title: download-artifact loses permissions on download
body:
The baseline behavior of the `zip` utilty on Linux and macOS is to retain permissions.

However, when the `download-artifact` action zips a directory, it loses permissions. With permissions broken and lost in the resulting asset zipfile, this subsequently breaks the artifacts for users or for downstream automated scripts.

Yes, one option is to write a _"github-download-permission-fixer"_ script that users must run after extracting the assets. However, this could be a lot of work to write and maintain, and hard to justify if it's simply to work-around broken behavior by GitHub.  Likewise, if you're dealing with multiple platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux), this script will need to be cross-platform and conform to the lowest-common-denominator available on all platforms (such as bash 3.x on macOS). The alternative is to ask users to install prerequisites (such as bash 4.x) before they can run the _github-permission-fixer_ script.

**Expected behavior**: permissions, as defined and applied by prior steps in the workflow to the resulting asset files and directories, should not be dropped or ignored by the `download-artifact` zipper, and should be present in the resulting asset zip file.
